subject: Computer Science
definition: Big-O notation describes an upper bound on how an algorithm's resource usage grows as the input size increases.
explanation: Big-O is commonly used to describe the growth rate of an algorithm's running time or space usage. For example, O(n) grows linearly with the input size, while O(n^2) grows quadratically.
examples: Scanning every element of an array once is typically O(n).
A nested loop that examines every pair of elements is typically O(n^2).
Binary search on a sorted array is O(log n).
common_mistakes: Thinking Big-O gives the exact execution time.
Ignoring how the algorithm scales when the input becomes larger.

subject: Computer Science
definition: Binary search finds an element in a sorted collection by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.
explanation: Binary search compares the target with the middle element. If the target is smaller, it searches the left half; if larger, it searches the right half.
examples: Searching for 42 in a sorted list by repeatedly checking the middle element.
common_mistakes: Using binary search on unsorted data.
Forgetting to update the search boundaries.
Assuming binary search works efficiently without ordering.

subject: Computer Science
definition: Linear search checks elements one by one until the target is found or the collection ends.
explanation: Linear search does not require the data to be sorted. In the worst case, every element may need to be examined.
examples: Searching for a name in an unsorted list by checking each name from the beginning.
common_mistakes: Assuming the data must be sorted.
Confusing linear search with binary search.

subject: Computer Science
definition: Recursion is a programming technique in which a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem.
explanation: A recursive solution normally contains a base case that stops recursion and a recursive case that reduces the problem toward the base case.
examples: Computing factorial using a recursive function.
common_mistakes: Failing to make progress toward the base case.
